common_name: Chromatella Water Lily (Classic Marliac Hardy Yellow Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; Chromatella, introduced by the historic Latour-Marliac nursery in the late 1800s, is one of the oldest and most widely grown hardy yellow water lily cultivars.

directions: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun. Chromatella was introduced by the historic French Latour-Marliac water lily nursery in the late 1800s and remains one of the most historically significant and widely sold hardy yellow water lily cultivars, producing star-shaped, canary-yellow flowers over attractively mottled, purple-blotched green foliage. Its long track record of reliable performance across a wide range of climates has kept it a standard recommendation for water gardens more than a century after its introduction. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the best bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: James Brydon Water Lily (Heat-Tolerant Hardy Rosy-Red Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; James Brydon is a classic hardy water lily noted for unusually strong heat tolerance, making it a recommended choice for warm Southern ponds.

directions: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun. James Brydon is a classic hardy water lily bearing cupped, rosy-red, peony-like double flowers over purplish-mottled green foliage, and it stands out among hardy water lilies for its unusually strong tolerance of hot summer water temperatures, which can cause many other hardy cultivars to stall or decline in flowering during the hottest part of the season. This heat tolerance has made it a long-recommended choice for water gardens across the warm South, including the Gulf Coast. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the best bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Charles de Meurville Water Lily (Classic Marliac Large Wine-Red Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; Charles de Meurville, a classic Marliac introduction, bears exceptionally large, deep wine-red to burgundy flowers on a vigorous plant.

directions: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun, allowing plenty of room for this vigorous cultivar to spread. Charles de Meurville is a classic French Marliac-bred hardy water lily producing exceptionally large, deep wine-red to burgundy star-shaped flowers with a subtle fragrance, among the largest and darkest-colored blooms of any hardy water lily cultivar, held above vigorous, spreading foliage that can quickly fill a good-sized pond. Its long history and dramatic bloom color have kept it a favorite for gardeners wanting a bold, dark accent in a water garden. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the best bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society
